reviews.title: 26.10 Update
reviews.text:
I feel deeply disappointed with the direction that the app is heading under the new ownership. 

iOS users have waited roughly one year for a new update, just to have an unwanted UI change that breaks existing functionality and makes studying much more tedious than before. 

I had purchased this app a couple of years ago to support the developers of this study tool, and it has undoubtedly been incredible for my studies in university, but I can no longer in good conscience recommend this app (i.e. on iOS) to my peers unless the community’s concerns are addressed.

I genuinely hope that this was a mistake and that the app will change for the better as we move forward. If that does happen, I will be happy to revert this to a five-star review.

It’s like one of those contests for designing the worst feature and this could be in it. It really needs to be fixed.

reviews.title: Redesign Is a Major Step Backward
reviews.text:
I’ve used AnkiMobile for years and have generally been very satisfied with it. Unfortunately, the latest update has made the browser substantially worse.

The new interface wastes an extraordinary amount of screen space. Where the old browser displayed a large number of cards at once, the new version shows only about six or seven, with enormous amounts of empty space between entries. Even disabling the additional card details does nothing to reduce the row height.

Searching has also become unnecessarily cumbersome, requiring additional taps to dismiss the search interface before the results can be viewed properly.

For those of us maintaining thousands of vocabulary cards, the ability to scan and navigate large numbers of entries quickly is essential. The redesign sacrifices precisely that functionality without any apparent benefit.

Please restore the old browser layout, or at least provide a compact-view option. AnkiMobile was an excellent application. This update has made it significantly less pleasant and efficient to use.

reviews.title: Anki was built for efficiency. What happened?
reviews.text:
This redesign is absolutely atrocious. It feels like the developers fundamentally misunderstand why people use Anki in the first place.

Anki is a STUDY TOOL. Its greatest strength has always been efficiency. The old interface was compact, straightforward, and information-dense. I could open the app, immediately see all my decks and their review counts, and get to work. Now everything is buried inside enormous rounded rectangles, unnecessary spacing, oversized menus, and endless scrolling. Information that previously fit on one screen now requires navigating an absurd amount of visual clutter.

Why on earth does every deck need to spell out “New,” “Learning,” and “To Review”? Anyone who has used Anki for more than a day understands what the colored numbers mean. We don’t need the interface holding our hands and wasting half the screen explaining them. Even the supposed compact mode doesn’t adequately address the wasted space.

This honestly looks like someone asked an AI to “make Anki look like a modern iOS app” and implemented the result without considering how people actually use the software. It’s design for the sake of design, with absolutely no regard for workflow efficiency.

I was already concerned when Damien Elmes stepped back from leading Anki’s development. This update has done nothing to inspire confidence in the new direction. Anki became successful because it prioritized FUNCTION over appearance. It was a powerful, practical tool that respected its users’ time.

reviews.title: Crashed and Burned
reviews.text: I’m sorry, but does not mean better. Did anyone who was a part of making or approving this new UI actually use it? I feel like we have a bunch of people who have never used Anki. Making you eyes for them flipping through it a little bit and yeah, this looks super cool, We should push it out. Well let me tell you as someone who does 2 to 300 flashcards a day this new UI is absolute garbage. Newer design does not always mean better. The entire point of the old Anki design was to get as much information as possible and as Little space as possible. You guys have taken the exact opposite approach now there’s a bunch of free space everywhere and all of the information is overly verbose and half of it doesn’t even fit. I don’t need verbose information if there’s an entire five minute learning curve to figure out how to use Anki, but that keeps things simpler that’s infinitely better than whatever this. And don’t even get me started on the search you have completely and totally destroyed your search functionality with this new UI. Not only is searching way more difficult because I have to click a bunch of extra buttons just to get the search button to actually do the search, but then when it finally does search, the results are completely useless. Not only do they not have a uniform shape anymore: field one for card a no longer reflects field one for card B because they thought that flipping that around would somehow be helpful (it’s not) but the information is also so overly verbose

reviews.title: I thought people were exaggerating how bad the UI is
reviews.text:
The UI is about as intuitive as the first 5 minutes of learning Microsoft excel is. It just feels like an overwhelming and jumbled mess of features glued on a screen haphazardly.

If you think you can merely add cards then swipe through them you are wrong. It’ll take you quite some time to figure out how to do even that.

Normally this wouldn’t be upsetting, but for $25 a pop you’d think they could afford to bring on a UI designer and make this in *some way* intuitive. 

There are many features, but you’ll spend 90% of your study time trying to reverse-engineer this goofily unintuitive design to locate them. Wack.

reviews.title: The most frustrating app experience ever!
reviews.text:
I have spent over 40 minutes trying to figure out how to do a basic task—importing a CSV or TXT file—and NOTHING works. This is easily the most unintuitive app I have ever used.
The app references an "iTunes link," which is completely outdated and irrelevant for a mobile app in 2026. For an app that is extremely expensive compared to others in the category, the UI feels 15 years old and the workflow is a nightmare. There is no direct "import" button for cloud files; instead, you’re stuck in a loop of "invalid zip" errors and "EOCD" messages just trying to load a simple spreadsheet.
I bought this expecting a premium experience, but instead, I got a headache. Extremely frustrating. I want my money back.

My advice to others is to try to determine if a flash card approach is right for you before you buy this app.

But, on iPhone?

This ‘app’ is 

Awkward;
The UI is terrible;

Why must I review 1,999 words to get back to the word I am learning as new?

Anki has been a waste of time on iPhone.
